subject: FineEdge Performance SLO - Benchmark Methodology Exchange
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finedge.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Performance & SLO qualification (thanks for the demo)

Alex — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of requirements we heard on the call:
- Latency: target P95 <= 120ms for 512-token streaming responses, P99 <= 300ms
- Concurrency: sustain 20 concurrent streaming sessions, with burst capacity to 100 sessions for up to 2 minutes
- Throughput: expected steady-state ~200 req/s for encoded prompts (peak 500 req/s burst)
- Streaming: yes — token-by-token streaming with low inter-token latency is required for your UX
- Reproducibility: benchmark must be repeatable across runs and capture model version + quantization details

Proposed next steps:
1) We’ll draft a benchmark methodology (workloads, prompt sets, measurement definitions, ramp/baseline).
2) You confirm the targets above and any additional constraints (auth, IP ranges, data retention).
3) Schedule a 60-minute kickoff to run an initial smoke benchmark and validate harness + metrics.

I’m attaching a first-pass benchmark plan and a small prompt set to kick things off (see attachments). Can you confirm: 1) the latency/throughput/concurrency targets above, and 2) a preferred date for the kickoff next week?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx)
(attachment: prompt_set_v1.jsonl)

From: Alex Johnson <alex@finedge.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FineEdge Ops <ops@finedge.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Performance & SLO qualification (thanks for the demo)

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side so your benchmark aligns with our production expectations:

1) Latency targets: the P95 <= 120ms target is correct for 512-token average responses when streaming. For longer responses (1024 tokens) we expect P95 <= 220ms — please include both token-length bins in the methodology.
2) Concurrency/throughput: sustain 20 concurrent streaming sessions (each session is typically a 1–3 request exchange). Peak bursts to 100 concurrent sessions are allowed for short periods; we expect sustained throughput of ~200 req/s with capacity to absorb spikes up to 500 req/s for < 5 minutes.
3) Streaming semantics: we stream partial tokens; inter-token latency matters — please include inter-token median and 95th percentile metrics.
4) Warm-up: ensure KV cache warm-up is accounted for — real traffic typically hits a warm cache after first minute.
5) Security/compliance: Ops will need the harness to run in an environment that meets our network allowlist and audit logging needs — I cc’d ops for visibility.

Also: can you confirm measurement definitions (how you compute p95/p99 for streaming sessions vs per-token measurements)?

If you can update the methodology with the above and share a runbook, we can target a kickoff on Mon 2026-03-15 09:00 PT.

—Alex
Head of Infrastructure, FineEdge
(ops contact included)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@finedge.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Performance & SLO qualification (benchmark methodology draft attached)

Alex — thanks for the detailed targets. Attached is a first-pass benchmark methodology and a more comprehensive prompt set (prompt_set_v1.jsonl) plus the harness bundle (eval_harness_v1.tar.gz). High-level notes from our side: 

- Workload bins: we’ll test 256 / 512 / 1024 token response lengths; each bin will have separate latency distributions.
- Measurement definitions:
  * Request-level: measure request start -> final token emitted. Compute p50/p95/p99 over requests (session-level aggregation for multi-request sessions).
  * Token-level (streaming): measure inter-token latency across emitted tokens; compute median and p95 inter-token latency.
  * Tail behavior: report server-side queueing/wait times, and percentage of responses exceeding SLOs.
- Warm-up and reproducibility:
  * 5-minute ramp, 10-minute steady run, repeat 3 iterations per bin.
  * Capture model hash, quantization profile, kernel selection, and RNG seed for each run.
- Environment: we will run on Redwood Dedicated test pool with GPU pinning and a reproducible container image. We’ll provide a runbook with exact container and harness config.

Attachments: benchmark_plan_v1.xlsx (detailed test plan), prompt_set_v1.jsonl (seeded prompts), eval_harness_v1.tar.gz (test harness + measurement scripts).

Could Vivek and Rishi confirm the recommended ramp/run durations and whether we should include a longer soak test for cache-impact scenarios? Also Alex — Ops, if you have allowlist ranges and retention/audit requirements, please send them and we’ll provision.

Next step: If you’re good, we’ll lock the kickoff for Mon 2026-03-15 09:00 PT and run the smoke test to validate metrics collection.

Thanks,
Marissa
(attachment: eval_harness_v1.tar.gz)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-04T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: internal: benchmark methodology notes

Quick internal notes on the methodology Marissa attached (feel free to forward to FineEdge):
- Warm-up: agree with 5-minute ramp, but recommend a short randomized burst at t=0 to prime KV caches across shards.
- Run lengths: 10-minute steady run is fine for initial smoke; for production-grade claims we should run a 60-minute soak for at least one iteration to observe cache behavior.
- Metrics: record both client-observed and server-observed timestamps to separate network jitter from server processing. Include per-GPU utilization and host-level logs in the harness.
- Reproducibility: capture container image sha, model weights sha, quantize flags, and random seed; store per-run artifacts in the Drive link.

I’ll prepare a short checklist for the kickoff (env vars, allowlists, node sizing).

-Vivek
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Johnson <alex@finedge.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FineEdge Ops <ops@finedge.ai>
Date: 2026-03-10T10:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FineEdge Performance SLO - Benchmark Methodology Exchange

Marissa/Vivek/Rishi — this looks good. Confirming the kickoff for Mon 2026-03-15 09:00 PT. A couple of final asks before we run: 

1) Can Redwood provide the harness image and a short runbook by EOD Thu 2026-03-12 so our Ops team can pre-configure allowlists and storage?
2) For the longer responses (1024 token bin) include the model variant and any quantization we plan to use in the initial run — we want to baseline against our prod variant.
3) Please include the exact commands you’ll use to compute p95/p99 so we can reproduce post-run.

Ops: I’ll share network allowlist and the audit retention window (we require 90-day logs for the run).

If those items are in place we’re aligned to proceed. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Alex Johnson
Head of Infrastructure, FineEdge
